payload.headline: Microsoft edges up to 496.13, holding above support; hold, swing trade stays on

summary.thesis: Microsoft's sales and margins are improving, but free cash flow is shrinking and the price already assumes heavy spending will pay off, so the stock looks fairly priced against its own history and expensive on cash flow.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, and add only at 475.73. Swing: stay in yesterday's trade, with new entries at 490.27, a stop at 475.34 and a target at 511.78.
summary.act_at: Add at 475.73; swing entry 490.27, stop 475.34, target 511.78

payload.happening: Microsoft closed at 496.13, up 0.74%. It stayed above the 485.58–490.27 support zone, which the price has touched 7 times, and it remains below the falling 20-day average of 518.38. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: The business itself is getting stronger. Quarterly sales grew 18.8% from a year earlier, slightly faster than the 18.3% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. Analysts have raised next-year earnings per share to 24.2 from 23.68 a month ago. The pressure is on cash. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after investment, fell to 60.0B from 78.0B. The filings say each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year, down from 51¢ three years ago, so the heavy spending is not paying back yet. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 29.0B and the share count shrank 0.27% over the year. What is at risk is the return on that spending, not demand or solvency. The 4 new risk headings in the annual report and the weak tech market (the macro read is a downtrend with elevated fear) affect sentiment, not the business.

worth.text: The valuation methods disagree sharply. A cash-flow model starting from today's 60.0B of free cash flow gives 180.81 to 288.62, with a base case of 218.43. To justify 496.13 on cash flow alone, free cash flow would have to start growing at about 39.7% a year. That is far above the 17% to 21% growth rates the model uses, and even 30% growth only gives 350.1. Measured against its own past price-to-sales, the stock looks fair: 475.73 at the low end, 535.43 in the middle and 592.92 at the high end. Today's price-to-sales of 10.6 sits at the 33rd percentile of its own 5-year range. Against peers it looks expensive, at 10.6 times sales versus a peer median of 3.5. The whole gap between the methods comes down to one question: does today's depressed cash flow describe the business, or will it recover as the spending matures? This note takes the own-history range from 475.73 to 535.43 and accepts that the cash-flow model is a real warning.
worth.key_assumption: The spending that cut free cash flow from 78.0B to 60.0B turns back into cash, so next-year earnings (estimate 24.2) are the right basis for value, not today's cash flow.

bull: Sales growth is speeding up a little: 18.8% from a year earlier last quarter, against 18.3% two quarters ago.
Estimates are rising: next-year EPS of 24.2 is up 2.2% in 30 days, which puts the price at 20.5 times next year's earnings versus 25.9 times trailing earnings.
Margins are improving: operating margin rose to 47.1% from 46.27%, and net cash is 29.0B.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and each invested dollar now earns 30¢ a year versus 51¢ three years ago.
The price implies about 39.7% starting cash-flow growth, while the cash-flow base case is 218.43 per share.
The price is 10.6 times sales against a peer median of 3.5, and the 20-day average (518.38) is still falling.

levels.what: Today's close sits inside the 475.73–535.43 fair range. Nothing here calls for selling, and it is not cheap enough to add.
The bottom of the own-history fair range, inside the 475.34–485.06 support zone (3 touches). This is the add level.
The bottom of the lower support zone. A close below it breaks both support zones and the fair range. In that case, no new adds until the 2027-01-27 report.

longterm.why: Growth, margins and estimates are improving, but free cash flow is shrinking and two of three valuation measures lean expensive. The plan is to hold, and to add only near 475.73.

swing.why: Yesterday's trade, triggered at 491.22, is still on, and the close of 496.13 held above the 485.58–490.27 zone (7 touches). New entries are at the top of that zone. The data's support zones have been redrawn, so the stop moves from 480.69 to 475.34, below both zones. That allows about one 16.71 average daily range. The target is the top of the 503.99–511.78 resistance zone. Taking part of the gain at 503.99 is reasonable, because the 20-day average is still falling.

decision.timing: The 2026-12-18 options price a 7.4% move, so the swing target fits inside that window. Any swing position closes before the 2027-01-27 report, which the 2027-02-19 options price at a 13.7% move. Long-term money beyond the 475.73 add waits for that report's free cash flow figure.

change_mind: A close below 475.34 breaks both support zones and the bottom of the fair range. That would end the swing trade and stop all long-term adds until the 2027-01-27 report.

If the 2027-01-27 report shows trailing free cash flow still at or below 60.0B, or quarterly revenue under the 96.7B estimate, the case for recovering cash weakens. The fair range would then shift toward the cash-flow values (218.43 base).
A close above 523.42, the top of the upper resistance zone and above the 50-day average of 518.63, would end the range. The swing target would then move beyond 511.78.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: hold, with the swing trade kept; the close of 496.13 held above the 485.58–490.27 support zone (7 touches), and only the swing stop moves from 480.69 to 475.34 because the support zones were redrawn.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
